status_summary: No law has repealed the diversity lottery, ended family-based categories beyond the immediate family or created a points system; bills have been introduced (H.R. 1241, 2025-02-12, repealing the diversity program, and H.R. 3466, 2025-05-15, a points-based system that would limit family categories to spouses and minor children and end the diversity program). Executive action reached the lottery: State postponed DV-2027 registration on 2025-11-05 and had not opened it by the end of FY2026, the Homeland Security Secretary announced a pause on 2025-12-18, and USCIS and State then held DV adjustment cases and paused DV visa issuance. On 2026-08-28 a federal court in California temporarily vacated those holds for FY2026 selectees and State said it was resuming issuance; a separate suit over DV-2027 registration awaited a ruling expected 2026-10-14. EO 14351 (signed 2025-09-19) created a Gold Card gift-based pathway using existing employment categories; the H-1B element is in c05-07.

timeline.event: H.R. 1241, the SAFE for America Act of 2025, was introduced; it would repeal the diversity immigrant program from 2025-10-01.

H.R. 3466, the Securing Migration, Addressing Reform, and Talent Retention Act, was introduced; by title it would create a points system, narrow family-based immigration and end the diversity visa program.
EO 14351 created a Gold Card program in which a gift of 1 million dollars (individual) or 2 million (corporate) counts as evidence for EB-1 and EB-2 categories.
State announced changes to the Diversity Visa entry process and postponed the start of DV-2027 registration.
The Homeland Security Secretary announced she was directing USCIS to pause the diversity visa program after a shooting suspect had entered through it.

USCIS placed a hold on pending Diversity Visa adjustment of status applications (PM-602-0193), and in December 2025 the State Department paused all visa issuance to Diversity Visa applicants to review screening and vetting.
timeline.source: N.D. Cal. order describing the policies

timeline.event: A law firm sued the Secretary of State in the Southern District of California to compel a DV-2027 registration process; a hearing was held 2026-09-24 and an oral ruling on a preliminary injunction was scheduled for 2026-10-14.

The Northern District of California (Medani v. Trump) certified subclasses of FY2026 Diversity Visa selectees and temporarily vacated the USCIS hold, the State Department pause and a separate 75-country pause as to them, finding them likely arbitrary and capricious.
The State Department said its December 2025 pause on diversity visa issuance was no longer in effect following the Medani court order and that it was resuming issuance.
